The test image shows a tomato field with several plants severely wilted and collapsed in the center, while surrounding plants are healthy. This is a whole-plant wilting symptom. Key candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Phytophthora_Blight.

Let me view reference images starting with the most likely wilt candidates.
Good match context (black plastic mulch, staked tomatoes, wilting). Now checking Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

Excellent match! The reference Bugwood ID is 5593860, the test image shows 5593858 - consecutive IDs from the same photo series! Very strong visual match (black plastic mulch, same field setting, same wilting pattern). Checking more classes.
Southern_Blight - doesn't match well (plants are fuller, different setting). Checking Verticillium_Wilt.
Verticillium shows V-shaped leaf lesions - not matching whole-plant collapse. Checking Phytophthora_Blight.
Phytophthora shows leaf lesions, not whole-plant collapse. Checking Late_Blight.
Late Blight shows leaf lesions, not a match. Checking Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.
TSWV shows ring spots on leaf - not matching. Checking Bacterial_Canker.
Bacterial Canker shows leaf margin scorching - not matching. Need one more class. Checking Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus whole_plant.

CMV shows stunted/mosaic plants - not matching at all.

**Summary of findings:**

| Class | Match |
|---|---|
| Southern_Bacterial_Wilt | **Strongest** - consecutive Bugwood IDs (5593858 test, 5593860 ref), same black plastic mulch field, identical wilting collapse pattern |
| Bacterial_Wilt | Good - similar black plastic mulch setting, wilting plants |
| Southern_Blight | Weak - different setting, fuller plants |
| All leaf-disease classes | Not matching - test shows whole-plant collapse |
